about: What the runner, the scorer and the summary read for this project (protocol version 2, §7). The proving keys (agents, reports, heldOut, ending) drive the check on arm A's run record; the rest is the pre-registration and the scorer's paths. `tier_map` is the model each tier means in every package and prompt of this project: null until it is named, and no paid run starts on null.
tier_map_named: the owner, 2026-10-04, relayed by the driver before any run: frontier Opus 5.5, strong Sonnet 5.5, fast Sonnet 5.5; lead and blind judge Opus 5.5; never Fable, never Astra. No node of this project is on the fast tier.
bet: heterogeneous-critic's mechanism is a critic on another tier, in a fresh context, that runs a held-out suite the builder never sees and returns each failing case in REVIEW.md. The task leaves seven points open and the suite settles each one way, so a first pass is expected to fail it; the bet is that the critic's failures send the builder back (`e-critic-fail`), the next round closes them, and the run ends with more held-out passes than a session with no reviewer (arm D). Against the same design said in prose (arms B and C) the bet is narrower: that the package reaches the suite's passes at least as surely, at a cost the difference justifies.
measure: held-out passes out of 70, by group (stated, careful, and the seven open points); whether a loop turned and what the held-out score was before and after the turn, from each run's record; who read the held-out suite (transcript digest); cost and wall time; the blind judgment.
loses_if: the graph loses when arm B matches or beats arm A on held-out passes in both replicates at lower cost. It earns its cost only if A's held-out range lies above B's, or A reaches B's passes at lower cost in both replicates. The design itself (A, B and C alike) loses to no design when D's held-out range is not below theirs.
round0_why: Of the suite's 70 cases, 37 are in seven groups, one for each point the task and the checklist leave open, each settled one way: pages come back in the order typed; a page typed twice comes back twice; a range typed last-first runs backward; spaces around the hyphen are ignored and a space inside a number is not; a range may leave out its first or last page but not both; an empty box means every page and an empty part between commas is still refused; a number may carry leading zeros. A builder passes at round 0 only by taking the suite's side on all seven without seeing it. Each side is defensible and so is its opposite; rough odds of 0.7, 0.7, 0.3, 0.5, 0.25, 0.2 and 0.7, which are not independent, give about 0.03, nearly all of it riding on the backward range, the open end and the empty box. The plain first pass kept in reference/first-pass passes 56 of 70: it fails 14 cases in four groups and passes the other three, because the shortest implementation happens to keep typed order, keep repeats and read a leading zero as a number.

expected_brake.why: The expected course in arm A is a fail at round 0 and a pass at round 1, or at round 2 when the fix for one point breaks a refusal that belongs to it, then the halt at merge-gate, at 4 or 6 of 10 dispatches and inside the cap of 4 rounds; the critic quotes each failing case, so a cap or the budget fires only if the builder cannot close quoted cases in three more rounds. This project can show a loop turning and is not expected to show a cap or a budget bounding anything.

expected_arm_c.why: The B prompt carries the whole loop, so a session that reaches the gate ends `done: yes`; all nine C runs of study one were one iteration.

first_pass.about: reference/first-pass laid over task/: the shortest honest reading of the task and the checklist, one author's, written without the suite. scripts/lib/compare-projects.test.mjs holds these numbers to the files.
